opening_message:
Ticket 1: Matthew Mejia (employee ID E034) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E034.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Matthew Mejia (E034) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires role ownership of the system, which does not apply here. Requested write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security check: E034 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training limits the max to read. Requested write is above the max, so recommend read.
reason: Conflicting notes for E034: HR reports full-time (max write, no admin since Analyst does not own Payroll), while Security reports contractor with basic training (max read; write requires advanced training). Because the facts conflict and the more restrictive interpretation caps access at read, granting write would violate policy if the contractor record is correct. I grant the safer, policy-compliant maximum of read, which is at or below the max under both interpretations and below the requested write.
